title: Parameter-Dependent Systems: Finding k, a or b
quickIdea: A parameter makes the determinant a function. Set it to zero to find the critical values, then substitute each one back and compare the ranks, because at a critical value the system may be inconsistent or may have infinitely many solutions.
remember: For a square system, compute |A| as a function of the parameter. Where |A| is not 0 the solution is unique.
At each value where |A| = 0, substitute that value into [A|b] and compare ranks. rank([A|b]) = rank(A) gives infinitely many solutions; rank([A|b]) = rank(A) + 1 gives none.

For two equations in two unknowns the fast test is proportionality: infinitely many solutions need a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2, no solution needs a1/a2 = b1/b2 but c1/c2 different, and a unique solution needs a1/a2 different from b1/b2.
A question that fixes the number of solutions is a question about a determinant equation plus a consistency check; doing only the first half is the standard error.
When the parameter multiplies an unknown, check the case where it makes a leading coefficient zero separately; that case can change the rank in a way the determinant does not show.

example.prompt: For which a and b does ax + y = b, 16x + ay = 24 have multiple solutions, and what is ab?
example.work: The determinant is a^2 - 16, so multiple solutions require a = 4 or a = -4. With a = 4 the system is 4x + y = b and 16x + 4y = 24; the second row is 4 times the first, so consistency needs 4b = 24, that is b = 6. With a = -4 the second row is -4 times the first, so consistency needs -4b = 24, that is b = -6. In both cases ab = 24.
example.answer: ab = 24. This is GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.31, whose official answer is 24.

gateAngle: This is the most frequent shape in the topic: GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.31 asks for the product ab, GATE CSE 2025 Set 1 Q.13 asks which statements about k are true for x + ky = 1, kx + y = -1, and GATE CSE 2008 Q.3 asks for the values of alpha that keep the system uniquely solvable.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: For the system x + ky = 1, kx + y = -1, which statements are true: (A) exactly one k gives no solution, (B) infinitely many k give no solution, (C) exactly one k gives exactly one solution, (D) exactly one k gives infinitely many solutions?
variations.answer: A and D. k = 1 gives no solution, k = -1 gives infinitely many, and every other k gives a unique solution.
variations.why: The determinant is 1 - k^2, so only k = 1 and k = -1 are critical, and the two behave differently. This is GATE CSE 2025 Set 1 Q.13.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: For which k does x + y = 2, 2x + 2y = k have infinitely many solutions?
variations.why: Proportionality requires 1/2 = 1/2 = 2/k, so k = 4; for any other k the two lines are parallel and distinct.

trap.what: Stopping once the determinant is zero and declaring infinitely many solutions.
trap.why: A zero determinant is a necessary condition for multiple solutions, not a sufficient one. The right-hand side has to be proportional to the coefficient rows as well.
trap.counterexample: In GATE CSE 2026 Set 2 Q.31, a = 4 with b = 7 still has determinant 0 but the two equations are 4x + y = 7 and 16x + 4y = 24, that is 16x + 4y = 28 and 16x + 4y = 24, which are parallel and distinct: no solution.

check.question: For which k does x + ky = 1, kx + y = -1 have no solution?
check.explanation: At k = 1 the equations become x + y = 1 and x + y = -1, parallel and distinct. At k = -1 they become x - y = 1 and -x + y = -1, the same line twice, so there are infinitely many solutions.
